sentences.text: Revenue rose from $1.66 billion in FY2022 to $5.39 billion in FY2025, a three-year CAGR of 48.1% [F4][F7][D342].
Operating margin improved from -413.5% in FY2022 to -66.5% in FY2025, yet the operating loss was still $3.59 billion [F28][F31][F26].
The FY2022 revenue jump of 2914.5% came primarily from 19,412 more vehicle deliveries [D83][P67].

Gross profit turned positive at $144 million in FY2025 from -$1.20 billion in FY2024, and the filing credits higher selling prices and lower cost per vehicle for the automotive improvement [F14][F13][P20].
Software and Services segment revenue grew 221.7% to $1.56 billion in FY2025, adding 21.6pp to total revenue growth [S26][D322][D323].
The filing attributes the increase to vehicle electrical architecture and software development services, remarketing sales, and repair and maintenance services [P18].
Automotive revenue fell 14.6% and subtracted 13.2pp from growth, leaving it at 71.1% of revenue versus 90.3% in FY2024 [D315][D316][D314][D311].
The automotive decline came from 9,332 fewer deliveries, due in part to the expiry of 45W tax credits, and lower regulatory credit sales [P22].
Diluted shares rose 17.1% in FY2025 while the net loss shrank 23.2%, so the per-share loss narrowed by 34.5% [D260][D241][D242].
FY2025 operating margin of -66.5% is the window high, against a median of -129.4% and a low of -7,672.7% in FY2021 [D325][D326][D324].
In the FY2025 bridge, cost of revenue added 26.8pp to operating margin, R&D added 1.5pp and SG&A subtracted 0.5pp [D267][D268][D269].
Cost of revenue fell 15.0%, which the filing ties to fewer vehicles produced and delivered and lower material and conversion costs [D255][P21].
Net margin of -67.7% sits below operating margin of -66.5% because other expense included $186 million for a securities class action settlement [F43][F31][P10].
Free cash flow was -$2.49 billion in FY2025 against a net loss of $3.65 billion, a free cash flow margin of -46.2% [F78][F38][D226].
Operating cash outflow narrowed to $779 million, which the filing attributes to a significant reduction in net loss [F64][P4].
Capex rose 49.9% to $1.71 billion, or 2.18x D&A, on expansion of production capacity at the Normal Factory [F71][D246][D228][P3].
Net cash fell to $1.64 billion in FY2025 from $3.26 billion in FY2024, with debt flat at $4.44 billion [D231][D179][F135].
Net cash at 30.5% of revenue ranks in the 75th percentile of four autos peers, above their 17.8% median [D232][D351][D352].
Financing inflow of $886 million came primarily from shares issued to Volkswagen Group and capital contributed by outside parties in Mind Robotics [F92][P2].
Diluted shares rose 17.1% in FY2025, after 7.0% in FY2024, so funding the burn is diluting holders [D260][D209].
Rivian has posted a net loss in each of seven years, including $3.65 billion in FY2025, and its accumulated deficit reached $27.0 billion [R1][F38][P5].
Stock-based compensation was 13.8% of revenue in FY2025 and at least 10% in each of the last five years [R2][D223].
Cash and investments of $6.08 billion cover 2.4 years of the latest burn, and the filing expects significant capital investment over the next several years [R3][D229][D236][P5].
Automotive was 71.1% of revenue and fell 14.6% in FY2025, with the filing citing fewer deliveries and expired 45W credits [R5][D314][D315][P22].
Product-axis revenue members overlap, so this analysis uses segment figures rather than adding product lines together [R6].
Gross margin staying above the FY2025 level of 2.7% would confirm the turn; a fall below it would reverse it, visible in the FY2026 10-K [F19].
Free cash flow burn below the FY2025 level of $2.49 billion would confirm narrowing losses, while burn above it would reverse the trend, visible in the FY2026 10-K [D235].
Automotive revenue growth above the FY2025 decline of 14.6% would confirm stabilisation, with R2 deliveries expected from the second quarter of 2026 [D315][P31].
